items.title: Mr. Meadow: Bitcoin Deserves Better Visuals
items.summary:
Mr. Meadow is a Bitcoin artist and filmmaker in India. He prices the work in sats. The site is mrmeadow.org.
He found Bitcoin in 2017 through a friend and bought some, then spent the next years on altcoins because he could not yet tell signal from noise. He designed for a friend's wallet company, spent time at Deloitte, and worked with a Polkadot India team that was training coders in Rust and chasing funding. She tells the story of earning a million sats in a single acoustic set, from people in the room and people watching online. items.title: Bitbrand: Bitcoin Saved My Life
items.summary:
Bitbrand makes hand-branded Bitcoin goods the old way: steel, fire, and leather. No ink, no printer, and no two pieces alike. He invented the Bitcoin branding iron, calls himself the branding iron broker, and built the company from the back of a van.
In this episode of Share Your Bitcoin Journey, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson meets Bitbrand in Jersey City, after they first met at the Midwest Bitcoin Summit in Columbus. Bitbrand tells how Bitcoin saved his life, how an ATM on the Upper East Side changed what he did with his money, and how he got sober at 30 and quit the corporate job

items.title: The Higher Low: Songs About Bitcoin That Never Say Bitcoin
items.summary:
Rami Korhonen has sung in the Finnish melodic punk band Fumble since the early nineties. One of their songs opens an episode of Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. A few years ago, on long business trips in the Middle East, he picked up a guitar he found in a rented apartment and started writing songs about Bitcoin, with one rule: the songs never say the word. He calls it acoustic pleb rock. The project is The Higher Low.

items.title: Chapter 4: Money as a Social Technology
items.summary:
The medium of exchange: a quiet reminder of how we think and feel... 

Excerpt from Chapter 4:
"In a fiat system –by virtue of its intrinsic characteristics and what it stands for– suspicion can but arise. Thereafter, an ever-continuing sequence of seemingly random events can but serve to condone the philosophical-political principle according to which “the end justifies the means”, rendering the prevailing monetary system utterly consistent. With sound money also, incentives can change, yet the interaction itself remains unaffected, because the medium of exchange has become neutral again. A change from fiat to sound money, then, reflects a dawning sense of value—or one that is already present."
As Bitcoiners, we cannot afford to carry fiat habits into a sound money paradigm, lest we taint even our noblest efforts with compromised means. Treat every transaction as a deliberate choice to uphold neutrality, vigilance, and what is truly at stake.

items.title: Self-Immolation to Self-Custody by Will Schoellkopf
items.summary: Nasser’s daughter is getting married on the beach in Beirut, and the bank won’t let him withdraw his own savings to pay for it. So he arrives with a pistol he has never fired, a can of petrol, and his ID. What happens next is a tense and darkly funny story about a desperate father and the money he can’t touch.

items.summary: It’s bond auction day, and the diner’s crowd gets thinner every week. Marvin sips his coffee and warns the waitress to pull out her cash and stock up on food, gold, silver, and lead. As the government locks down the banks and the economy teeters, the question is whether being right about the collapse will be enough to survive it.

items.summary: A seaside village is dancing to live jazz when a drone carrier blots out the sun with a 24-hour eviction notice from the Earth Central Bank. The villagers have three options: comply, fight, or take the Bank to a court run by bots that always rule for it. One young woman refuses to accept that the game is rigged.

items.title: The Big Slash by DJ Bodden
items.summary: You’re bagging your groceries when your payment is declined, and so is everyone else’s. Overnight, your money, your identity, your degree, even the lock on your door vanish with a dead chip in your palm. In a world where owning anything now means someone else’s permission, one ordinary man has to work out who he is when the keys to his life stop working.

items.title: Financial Fallout
items.summary:
Currencies debased. 
Privacy under attack. 
Cash goes underground. 
The crushing weight of debt. 
We were never prepared. 

Welcome to a system designed to keep us poor. The harder we work, the less we gain.
And as we struggle, the noose only tightens. 
And then, when we have nothing left to lose, we turn on those who rigged the game. 
We stand and fight. 

These 21 stories portray unfortunate yet brilliant heroes fighting the powers that triggered financial fallout. Money is broken, but hope is not lost.

***

DM for access to access to a Underworld, a bonus story by Max Hillebrand.
